# Question

**How broadly do experiences of parents affect their future children?** Ng et al. (2010, *Nature*) put founder male rats on a high-fat diet, mated them, and raised the F1 daughters on standard chow — isolating the paternal *pre-conception* environment from anything postnatal.

## Data source

Seeded rescale (n = 34 rows) to the paper's published mean ± SEM group summaries; per-animal raw data are not public, so p-values approximate the paper's. Fathers: 8 control vs 9 high-fat.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Daughter insulinogenic index (6 wk) by father's diet"
off = df[df["cohort"] == "offspring"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 4))
sns.boxplot(data=off, x="father_diet", y="insulinogenic_index",
            hue="father_diet", palette=["#8fbf8f", "#c76c6c"], legend=False, ax=ax)
sns.stripplot(data=off, x="father_diet", y="insulinogenic_index",
              color="0.25", size=4, ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("Father's diet")
ax.set_ylabel("Insulinogenic index (daughter, 6 wk)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Welch t-tests for father manipulation checks; two-sample comparisons with Cohen's d, 100k-replicate randomization and bootstrap CIs for offspring endpoints.

| Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| Fathers: body weight (manipulation check) | 705 g vs 550 g, d = −3.45, p ≈ 3.6e-6 |
| Daughter insulinogenic index | 38.7 vs 86.8 (halved), d = 2.58, randomization p = 0.0004 |
| Daughter glucose peak (6 wk) | impaired, p = 0.023 |
| Islet gene expression | 56 / 77 genes down-regulated, p = 6.6e-05 |
| Daughter body weight (12 wk) | unaffected, p = 0.47 |

# Decision

Paternal high-fat diet **reprograms daughter β-cell function without obesity** — the effect is specific (insulin secretion / glucose tolerance), not a generalized growth effect. A clean experimental demonstration of intergenerational metabolic programming (reconstruction caveat applies).
